title: Photo 199 · 콜로설 · 라이롯남 · 무릎 꿇기 3/4 (양 무릎) · 흑인 40대 후반
prompt:
Image format: a vertical portrait-orientation photograph, 2:3 aspect ratio, taller than it is wide.

A full-body photograph on a plain seamless mid-grey backdrop, nothing in the frame but a low flat platform, shot on a medium format camera with an 85mm lens at f/8, a single hard key light raking in from one side so the texture of the skin stands out, sharp focus from head to toe, realistic photographic grain — a real photograph, not an illustration, not CGI, not a render.

Subject: ONE real adult Black woman in her late 40s, faint lines at the eyes and mouth, deep near-black skin tone, THE ABSOLUTE DARKEST BLACK SKIN ON EARTH, void complexion, not brown, not lightened, her face exactly as dark as her body, real skin texture with visible pores and fine grain, a voluminous curly half-up half-down style, a calm confident expression, real living eyes. She wears long geometric drop earrings and has oval nails with a satin finish.

Physique: An extraordinarily large woman, far beyond any real person, her body so wide that her hips are cut off by the left and right edges of the frame. A giantess built on a completely even scale, every part of her enlarged by the same amount: massive rounded shoulders, huge thick arms, a colossal full bust, a broad heavy torso with a large smooth rounded belly, wide solid hips, enormous columnar thighs and thick heavy calves, a full round face. Her head looks small on top of her massive body, her shoulders span more than four head-widths, each hand is as wide as a normal woman's torso and each thigh thicker than a normal woman's waist. No single part stands out more than another, no hanging folds, not pregnant, her whole body scaled up together into one immense smooth silhouette that towers over the viewer. Every fold and curve keeps its own clear rounded outline with a deep shadowed crease between them, never merging into one shapeless mass. Her arms, hands, legs and feet stay in correct proportion to each other. The flesh is softer and looser at this age, each fold hanging lower and settling further over the one below it. The sheer weight of the flesh is visible in how it drops, settles and presses down onto the thighs beneath it.

Skin: Real photographic skin — visible pores and fine grain, a coarser surface grain, natural creases and shadow where the flesh folds, crepey texture in the deepest folds, faint stretch marks where the great curves have expanded, the raking light picking out every ridge and hollow of the surface. No smooth illustration finish, no plastic CG sheen.

Body Art: Her bare skin is painted in Thai lai rot nam style — brilliant gold leaf over a black lacquer ground, continuous kranok flame scrolls covering every surface, a gold border band following every deep crease and curving around the hips and thighs, kranok scrolls filling the space between every band. The paint is pigment sitting on living skin, so it distorts slightly over every bulge and cracks a little where the skin folds. The paint covers her whole body with no bare skin left anywhere below the jaw: her shoulders, her upper arms, her forearms and the backs of her hands are painted as densely as her torso, and so are the sides of her body, her back, her rear, the lower belly, the knees, the calves and the tops of her feet. Her face is left unpainted and the pattern fades out at the neck with no hard line.

Pose: Kneeling upright on the platform and turned about 45 degrees from the camera with the front of her body still mostly toward the lens, her face toward the camera, both shins and feet folded back beneath her and her weight settled onto her heels, her knees wide apart, her back straight, her near hand resting on her thigh and her far arm held back so nothing crosses in front of her torso, the enormous rounded rear settling back onto her heels seen in partial profile, full body head to knees filling the frame.

Footwear: Extreme gold platform stiletto sandals laced around the ankle, the platform soles as tall as her ankle bones, the ultra-thin stiletto heels so high her insteps stand nearly vertical.

Background & Lighting: the gold leaf blazing, catching the light the way gold paint on skin does rather than like solid metal, the hard raking light carving every fold and curve.

Vertical 2:3 portrait-orientation full-body photograph, taller than it is wide.
